title: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work
body: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work Oct 28, 2026 | Tina Schuchman CVP, Foundry and Vladimir Fedorov, CTO, GitHub If you want to compete, you need to be multi-model. And if you want to take advantage of everything that different AI models have to offer, you need a great harness. But building one that works seamlessly across multiple models and surfaces is incredibly hard. You need to solve for performance, quality, and cost. And then you have to maintain it, which is even harder. Luckily, the GitHub engineering team built a best-in-class, truly multi-model harness , which we’ve adopted company-wide. The Microsoft Copilot harness powers Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, the GitHub Copilot app, the CLI, VS Code, and more. And today, we’re making that harness available through Microsoft Foundry . That gives developers and enterprise customers a fully managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. You get the right model for the job without switching the harness or the rest of your tech stack. That frees up your time, energy, and resources to focus on your bottom line. What’s a harness, and why is it hard? If the model supplies the intelligence, the harness is everything around the model. It’s the orchestration layer that gives an agent the right instructions, context, execution environment, and controls to accomplish meaningful work. And a harness worth its salt has support for open standards like MCP and agent skills, as well as agent plugins. This is a fast-moving space. A frontier model today might fall behind tomorrow. And building your own harness or model router to keep up can be painful and slow. Now, you can build on the same harness Microsoft and GitHub ship in our own products, and you don’t have to maintain it. We invest in science and engineering work to continually improve and evolve the harness and ensure high-quality, efficient, and low-cost performance across a range of models and workloads. The benefits compound for us and our customers who use the harness to build and run their own agents. Improve the harness, and every surface it touches benefits. Born in GitHub, battle-tested at enterprise scale The Copilot harness was built by the same GitHub engineers behind new technologies like our multi-model orchestration . And those technologies are only possible because we built our own harness. Designed to be fast, token-efficient, and predictable, it was our original, high-quality harness. And it had the highest satisfaction among our most demanding audience: developers. That’s why we’re standardizing all of our Copilot experiences on the strongest foundation possible. The harness is built to perform across model families , with 20+ frontier models plus bring your own key, so you can use the right model for the right job. Instead of doing the work to keep up with and eval new models, lean on us to intelligently route work to the right model or models based on the task. Our harness is flexible and configurable to any type of app, agent, or service. We recently ported the harness runtime to Rust , which has resulted in industry-leading performance and reductions in both session overhead and time-to-first token. And because the Copilot harness powers surfaces across Microsoft, it’s battle-tested and proven performant at the scale of millions of users and hundreds of real-world use cases. A unified harness lets us ship faster, learn faster, and improve Copilot over time. And because the agents you build in Foundry can run on the same harness we’ve adopted across Microsoft, our continuous harness improvements will benefit your agents, too. Try it yourself The SDK is available to download , or you can run the harness in the cloud, all managed by Foundry. Our platforms remain open and interoperable, so you can continue to bring in any harness and framework you want, too. With the Copilot harness, Microsoft runs the agent loop and sandbox, with governance and optimization built in from day one. You bring the instructions, skills, tools, and model choice. This is an important step towards our vision of a stronger system around the model that preserves choice. It represents the best of GitHub, brought to the Microsoft platform and beyond. We’ll keep pushing the harness forward, so you can focus on what only you can build. Tags: GitHub , GitHub Copilot , Microsoft Copilot , Microsoft Foundry

title: Thin, Light and Built for Everything: NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows Laptops Gain New Models, Agent Tools and Games
body: Thin, Light and Built for Everything: NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows Laptops Gain New Models, Agent Tools and Games NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Liquid AI’s LFM3 models arrive for local AI; plus, Hermes Agent adds NVIDIA OpenShell and Switchyard, and ‘Phantom Blade Zero’ launches with NVIDIA DLSS 4.5. October 28, 2026 by Shreevar Rastogi 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA RTX Spark powers thin and light laptops built for everything that developers, creators and gamers do. RTX Spark laptops are now available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI. These powerful systems combine an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and an NVIDIA Grace CPU in a single superchip with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance. That puts the NVIDIA CUDA platform, RTX graphics and the capabilities of a personal AI supercomputer inside premium Windows laptops built to go anywhere. New and expected RTX Spark updates, coming soon, include: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open weight speech model for transcription, speaker attribution and translation is available on RTX Spark. The LFM3 family of open models with day-zero support. Resource management controls in NVIDIA App to allocate GPU resources between foreground apps and background agents. Phantom Blade Zero , S-GAME’s highly-anticipated action role-playing game, launches with ray tracing and NVIDIA DLSS 4.5. Experience Minecraft with path tracing and DLSS with RTX Remix1.6, available now for RTX Spark. Turn Recorded Audio Into Useful Information With NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe Introduced today, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a new, open weight speech model that turns recorded conversations into useful information. Instead of needing multiple models for transcription, speaker labels and translation, developers can use one promptable model that handles all three, plus questions about the audio. It transcribes 40 languages, including seven Indic languages. Developers guide the model with plain-language prompts. For example, for a single recorded meeting, users can ask it to: “Transcribe this recording and label each speaker.” “Translate this audio into English.” “List what decisions were made in this meeting.” Prompts can also include product terms and formatting conventions, which helps the model handle specialized vocabulary in fields like healthcare, financial services and customer service. Because the weights are open, developers can choose where audio is processed, from a desktop to the cloud. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe ranks No. 1 on the Hugging Face Open ASR and No. 2 among open weight models on Artificial Analysis — delivering leading accuracy with approximately 4.3 billion active parameters, 80% fewer than the No. 1 open weight model, making high-quality, intelligent transcription more practical on local hardware. It’s available today on Hugging Face in the BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 formats, and offers flexible deployment options for developers with support on NVIDIA RTX Spark, DGX Spark systems and Jetson AGX Thor devices. Developers can deploy NVFP4 versions through NeMo-Speech.cpp or vLLM. Learn more in the NVIDIA technical blog . Control How Agents and PC Apps Share GPU Resources On RTX Spark, users can have long-running agents working alongside their favorite applications. Both share the system’s GPU compute, and the right balance of resources depends on what matters to users at that moment. With the new resource management feature in NVIDIA App , users can now choose how GPU resources are shared. They can prioritize their foreground app for the best performance, or give their background-running agent more resources to get work done faster. Access control resource sharing from System > Advanced in the NVIDIA App. This feature requires hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling to be enabled in Windows Settings. Liquid AI : One Model Family, Many Ways to Work Liquid AI’s LFM3 provides a new generation of Liquid Foundation Models designed for specialized tasks. The family spans text, vision, audio, omni and decision models built on one shared backbone, with base and post-trained models available as open weights. The models are compact and fast: Liquid AI’s new 1.7-billion-parameter base model outperforms its previous 2.6-billion-parameter base model. These models support local workflows such as agents running in Hermes Agent, Pi and OpenClaw to triage inboxes and manage calendars, read documents and app screens, transcribe and translate speech, answer spoken questions about handwritten math, and route support tickets or voice requests. Developers can run LFM3 models on RTX Spark with native support through llama.cpp and vLLM, and fine-tune the models locally. ‘Phantom Blade Zero’ Launches With DLSS 4.5 S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero launches tonight, Oct. 28, at 7 p.m. PT on Steam and the Epic Games Store . Players can take on the role of Soul, a swordsman framed for his master’s murder, as he travels the martial world to uncover a conspiracy. NVIDIA worked with S-GAME Studio and S-GAME Publishing to add ray-traced effects to the title. On RTX Spark laptops and GeForce RTX GPU-powered PCs, ray tracing adds more accurate bounced lighting, detailed reflections and realistic shadows on foliage and terrain. The NVIDIA DLSS Dynamic Multi Frame Generation feature boosts frame rates with up to 6x frame generation, or adjusts the multiplier on the fly to hit a player’s target frame rate. Read more on GeForce.com . RTX Remix Breathes New Life Into Classics NVIDIA RTX Remix , the modding platform for remastering classic games with path tracing and DLSS, released version 1.6 last week. This update brought RTX Remix to the world’s largest gaming community: Minecraft . Both creators and players can render Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1 through RTX Remix with DLSS-accelerated path tracing and take full advantage of realistic lighting and materials in their future creations. The update also adds DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, up to 6x Multi Frame Generation, native RTX Spark support and agent-assisted workflows. Starting today, those upgrades come to Portal with RTX and the Half-Life 2 RTX demo. Both now support RTX Spark, with DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering for more lifelike lighting and materials, a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation and new options that speed up path tracing. RTX Remix 1.6 also makes AI-powered modding simpler. A redesigned ComfyUI workflow lets modders generate physically based materials directly inside RTX Remix, with no application programming interface setup, batch processing for full projects and presets for less technical creators. Plus, with NVIDIA agent skills, compatible AI agents can work directly with RTX Remix to help speed up remastering projects. Learn more in the RTX Remix blog . RTX Spark Laptops: Beautifully Designed, Built for Everything RTX Spark laptops come in a range of designs, so users can choose one that fits how they work and play. Options include different screen sizes, colors, touchscreens, pen support and two-in-one convertibles. RTX Spark laptops are as thin as 14mm and as light as three pounds, with all-day battery life. Such slim designs are possible because RTX Spark places the GPU, CPU and up to 128GB of unified memory on one power-efficient superchip. Creative projects and AI models draw from the same memory pool, so a laptop can take on work that used to call for a desktop workstation, even when unplugged. Here’s what this means for: AI developers: Run models and agents locally on NVIDIA CUDA — the same platform that powers AI in the cloud — with a path to deploy across more than 150 million NVIDIA RTX AI PCs and NVIDIA GPUs in the cloud. Creators: RTX Spark can edit camera native 4:2:2 video and render 3D scenes of up to 90GB. Adobe Photoshop and Premiere offer native RTX Spark support through beta releases. Gamers: Hundreds of games run on RTX Spark, with NVIDIA DLSS, ray tracing, Reflex and G-SYNC delivering sharper visuals and smoother, more responsive gameplay. RTX Spark laptops are available now from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599, with 128GB configurations on shelves. Find a laptop on the RTX Spark product page . #ICYMI: More Updates From NVIDIA Local AI 🦆Microducks learn to walk with help from RTX Spark: During the GTC Berlin keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed how AI agents running on RTX Spark can help train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot . A new NVIDIA technical blog walks through the workflow: Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt plan an obstacle course on RTX Spark, Astra builds the 3D assets, NVIDIA Isaac Lab trains the navigation policy and RTX Spark validates it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Watch the demo and try the playbook . ⚡ NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is now available , enabling natural conversations and multistep agent tasks with as little as 4GB of memory. The model powers local voice assistants, game characters and embedded interfaces on RTX Spark, DGX Spark, GeForce RTX GPUs and NVIDIA Jetson devices. It supports llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio, and works with Hermes and OpenClaw. For more demanding agent workloads, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run local agents on RTX Spark. 🖼️Black Forest Labs’ FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6-billion-parameter open weights model that lets users generate and edit images locally. NVIDIA-optimized versions run on RTX GPUs with as little as 8GB of VRAM. Developers can also fine-tune the model on RTX Spark using an NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel recipe to customize it for specific creative workflows. 🖥️ NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB is now available to purchase from manufacturer partners, giving developers and researchers another way to build and run AI locally. Powered by the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, it combines 64GB of unified memory with DGX OS and the NVIDIA AI software stack for agent development, inference and fine-tuning. Learn more and explore purchase options . Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X , Instagram , TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter . Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X . See notice regarding software product information. RTX Spark Laptops: Beautifully Designed, Built for Everything RTX Spark laptops come in a range of designs, so users can choose one that fits how they work and play. Options include different screen sizes, colors, touchscreens, pen support and two-in-one convertibles. RTX Spark laptops are as thin as 14mm and as light as three pounds, with all-day battery life. Such slim designs are possible because RTX Spark places the GPU, CPU and up to 128GB of unified memory on one power-efficient superchip. Creative projects and AI models draw from the same memory pool, so a laptop can take on work that used to call for a desktop workstation, even when unplugged. Here’s what this means for: AI developers: Run models and agents locally on NVIDIA CUDA — the same platform that powers AI in the cloud — with a path to deploy across more than 150 million NVIDIA RTX AI PCs and NVIDIA GPUs in the cloud. Creators: RTX Spark can edit camera native 4:2:2 video and render 3D scenes of up to 90GB. Adobe Photoshop and Premiere offer native RTX Spark support through beta releases. Gamers: Hundreds of games run on RTX Spark, with NVIDIA DLSS, ray tracing, Reflex and G-SYNC delivering sharper visuals and smoother, more responsive gameplay. RTX Spark laptops are available now from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599, with 128GB configurations on shelves. Find a laptop on the RTX Spark product page . #ICYMI: More Updates From NVIDIA Local AI Microducks learn to walk with help from RTX Spark: During the GTC Berlin keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed how AI agents running on RTX Spark can help train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot . A new NVIDIA technical blog walks through the workflow: Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt plan an obstacle course on RTX Spark, Astra builds the 3D assets, NVIDIA Isaac Lab trains the navigation policy and RTX Spark validates it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Watch the demo and try the playbook . NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is now available , enabling natural conversations and multistep agent tasks with as little as 4GB of memory. The model powers local voice assistants, game characters and embedded interfaces on RTX Spark, DGX Spark, GeForce RTX GPUs and NVIDIA Jetson devices. It supports llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio, and works with Hermes and OpenClaw. For more demanding agent workloads, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run local agents on RTX Spark. Black Forest Labs’ FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6-billion-parameter open weights model that lets users generate and edit images locally. NVIDIA-optimized versions run on RTX GPUs with as little as 8GB of VRAM. Developers can also fine-tune the model on RTX Spark using an NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel recipe to customize it for specific creative workflows. NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB is now available to purchase from manufacturer partners, giving developers and researchers another way to build and run AI locally. Powered by the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, it combines 64GB of unified memory with DGX OS and the NVIDIA AI software stack for agent development, inference and fine-tuning. title: Indie Games Fund in Africa: Meet the selected studios
body: Indie Games Fund in Africa: Meet the selected studios Oct 28, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Google Play has selected 10 independent game studios across Sub-Saharan Africa for the 2026 Indie Games Fund Africa, providing $1 million in non-dilutive funding, mentorship, and technical support to help scale local talent and bring authentic African games to a global audience. Nicola Julius Head of Ecosystem and Core Partnerships EMEA, Google Play Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Indie Games Fund Africa: Meet the selected studios Sub-Saharan Africa is home to some of the world's most vibrant storytelling, cultural richness, and creative ingenuity, powering one of the fastest-growing game development ecosystems on the planet. Earlier this year, we opened applications for the first-ever Google Play Indie Games Fund in Africa, committing $1 million to help bridge the funding gap, overcome international distribution barriers, and support talented indie developers across the continent. Today, we are thrilled to announce the 10 independent game studios selected for the 2026 cohort. Each of these studios will receive a share of non-dilutive funding, alongside direct access to commercial and growth resources, hands-on 1:1 mentorship from Google Play specialists, and tailored technical support from Unity. This support is designed to help them optimize their titles, scale sustainably, and bring authentic African stories and gameplay mechanics to a worldwide audience. Meet the 10 selected studios From action platformers, cozy puzzles, and rhythm games to immersive simulations, meet the studios shaping the future of African gaming: Clockwork Acorn (South Africa): A South African indie game studio founded in 2014 by industry veterans dedicated to making timeless games, supporting local talent, and creating a positive impact through their work. Jetstream is an elegant puzzle game featuring over 100 hand-crafted levels, a calming minimalist art style, and unique mechanics that challenge players to guide a plane through the clouds. Deluxe Entertainment Studios (Nigeria): An independent studio creating distinct games featuring striking visuals, bold ideas, and unique stories rooted in African imagination for global audiences. Their title Rasta Santa is an action-packed 2D platformer set in Lagos, where you play as an undercover cop disguised as Santa, waging war on traffickers to rescue children and defend an orphanage. Disputed People (South Africa): A South African studio founded in 2023 that is dedicated to crafting rich, character-driven video games filled with creativity, quality, and wonder-filled experiences. Their title Mitts and the Divine Recipes is a 3D retro-inspired adventure game where players explore the cozy world of Epicuria, gathering divine ingredients, cooking meals to gain special abilities, and solving puzzles to advance. Fer Factor (Nigeria): An independent game development studio based in Lagos, Nigeria, dedicated to crafting fun, innovative, and memorable gaming experiences for players worldwide. Their title Chore Master is a cozy and satisfying game where players use intuitive controls to clean spaces, scrub stains, and transform chaotic rooms into spotless, picture-perfect environments. Gazuntype Entertainment (Nigeria): The independent game development alias of Tade Ajiboye, an innovative builder with over a decade of experience crafting immersive video games and VR experiences in Nigeria. Their title Go North is a cozy, story-driven exploration adventure where players guide Dara through beautifully unique mazes, discover magical items, and uncover a sinister mystery. Leti Games Limited (Ghana): A pioneering African creative technology studio based in Ghana, dedicated to bringing authentic African stories and innovations to global audiences through games and interactive experiences. Their title Sweave is a rhythm-based, hyper-casual mobile game inspired by traditional African weaving techniques, where players navigate a dynamic weaving ball across a digital loom while dodging cultural obstacles and battling bosses. Maliyo Games (Nigeria): A Lagos-based studio founded in 2012 that creates engaging, African-inspired gaming experiences celebrating local culture for a global audience. Their title Safari City is a vibrant mobile puzzle and renovation game where players solve match-3 puzzles and restore a rundown town into a beautiful, thriving community. Studio Bo (South Africa): An animation and games company based in Cape Town, South Africa, known for bringing a playful visual style and quirky humor to interactive experiences, animations, and upcoming mobile titles. Their title Idle Sands is a cozy 2D idle-clicker where players manage a fleet of robots to clean up a beach, uncover treasures, and automate their operations with relaxing music and charming artwork. Vetkoek Studios (South Africa): A youth-owned South African game development studio dedicated to creating high-quality, accessible mobile games with authentic African themes while empowering the next generation of local creators. Their title Taxi Ranked is a casual, retro-style driving game capturing the chaos and humor of South African minibus taxis through vibrant comic-book graphics, multiple game modes, and deep vehicle customization. Weza Interactive (Kenya): A Kenyan game studio founded by twin brothers Odongo George Ahere and James Ahere to build original, culturally rich worlds that educate, empower, and entertain global audiences. Their title Riziki is a free-to-play mobile rhythm adventure where players guide twins Nabo and Moja across Africa, tapping and swiping to Afrobeats, Amapiano, and Rhumba to restore harmony and bring vibrant environments to life. Congratulations to all 10 studios. We're excited to champion your vision as you continue crafting unforgettable experiences for players around the world. Posted in:

title: Russian Woman Charged With Federal Hate Crimes For Stabbing Multiple Jewish Individuals
body: Press Release Russian Woman Charged With Federal Hate Crimes For Stabbing Multiple Jewish Individuals Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of New York United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, Assistant Director in Charge of the New York Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”), James C. Barnacle, Jr., and the Commissioner of the New York City Police Department (“NYPD”), Jessica S. Tisch, announced today that ANNA MOCHALOVA was arrested on charges of committing hate crimes in connection with her assaults of two Jewish men in and around the Diamond District in Manhattan on October 21, 2026.  MOCHALOVA was transferred from state custody earlier today and will be presented in Manhattan federal court before U.S. Magistrate Judge Robert W. Lehrburger. “This Office will continue to seek justice for victims of hate-based crimes and will aggressively prosecute those who seek to spread bigotry through violence,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald.  “As alleged, Anna Mochalova deliberately and viciously targeted Jewish victims with violence.  Mochalova allegedly stabbed two men specifically because they were Jewish, an attack made all the more terrifying because the specific weapon used—and its potential contents—remain unknown pending further investigation. Mochalova’s alleged actions were an attack on the fundamental right to freely and safely express one’s religious identity in public.” “Acts of hate and harassment have no place in our city,” said FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle, Jr. “The alleged hate-motivated crimes committed against Jewish members of our community are unacceptable and have no place in New York.  We will continue to use the full force of the law to protect the safety, security, and rights of every New Yorker, including members of our Jewish community.” “A hate crime is a message written in violence, and this defendant’s message was loud and clear,” said NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch.  “As alleged in the complaint, Anna Mochalova attacked two visibly Jewish New Yorkers, striking fear in an entire community.  Every New Yorker has the right to walk our streets safe from hatred and violence, and the NYPD will always hold those who threaten that right accountable.  I thank the NYPD investigators and our federal partners for responding swiftly to this unacceptable act of hate.” As alleged in the Complaint and other public filings: [1] On or about October 21, 2026, MOCHALOVA attacked two Jewish men in quick succession with a sharp object that is consistent with being a needle in and around the Diamond District in Manhattan.  First, at approximately 5:50 p.m., Victim-1, a Jewish man, was walking along West 47th Street between Fifth and Sixth Avenues when he noticed MOCHALOVA following him and speaking in Russian.  Shortly thereafter, MOCHALOVA stabbed Victim-1 in his lower back with a sharp object, which Victim-1 described as the feeling of a needle prick. At the time, Victim-1, who has a beard, was wearing attire traditionally worn by Orthodox Jewish men, including a black hat, a black suit, a white shirt, and tzitzit. MOCHALOVA then stalked past him towards Sixth Avenue.  A still image of the assault is depicted below: Shortly thereafter, MOCHALOVA approached Victim-2 and a second man (“Individual-1”), who were standing together on the northeast corner of Sixth Avenue and West 45th Street, approximately two blocks south of the location where Victim-1 was assaulted. Victim-2 and Individual-1 are also Jewish men, and both were wearing yarmulkes when MOCHALOVA approached. MOCHALOVA bumped into Victim-2 multiple times. As Victim-2 started to confront MOCHALOVA about her repeated bumps, he observed MOCHALOVA stab him with a sharp object on his right forearm. Victim-2, who speaks Russian, recalls that MOCHALOVA spoke in Russian and told him, in sum and substance, “run away, I have a gun.” MOCHALOVA also asked Individual-1, in sum and substance, if he was Jewish. Individual-1 responded, in sum and substance, “I don’t know, I’m Muslim?” MOCHALOVA told Individual-1 that she “was so sorry” and then fled northbound on Sixth Avenue. *                *                * MOCHALOVA, 32, of Russia, is charged with two counts of committing hate crimes, each of which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. The statutory maximum sentences in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendant will be determined by a judge. Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative work of the FBI and the NYPD. The prosecution of this case is being handled by the Office’s Civil Rights and Human Trafficking Unit in the Criminal Division, with consultation from the Criminal Section of the Civil Rights Division.  Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kaiya Arroyo and Christian Ronald are in charge of the prosecution. The charges contained in the Complaint are merely allegations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. Contact Nicholas Biase, Shelby Wratchford (212) 637-2600 Updated October 28, 2026 Attachment u.s._v._mochalova_-_sealed_complaint.pdf Topics Civil Rights Human Trafficking Component USAO - New York, Southern Press Release Number: 26-305

title: Two Men Ordered to Pay $86,000 in Total Fines and Restitution for Illegal Deer Hunting Operation in Fayette County
body: Press Release Two Men Ordered to Pay $86,000 in Total Fines and Restitution for Illegal Deer Hunting Operation in Fayette County Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Tennessee Jackson, TN – A federal judge has ordered Austin Elrod , 30 , of Somerville, Tennessee, to surrender his hunting license for 5 years and to pay a total of $60,000 for an illegal deer hunting operation. D. Michael Dunavant, United States Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee, announced the sentence today. An investigation by several law enforcement agencies revealed that Elrod was guiding white-tailed deer hunts in the Fayette County area without the required guiding license. The guided hunts were advertised on Facebook and resulted in the illegal harvesting of seven deer throughout the 2021 and 2022 hunting seasons. Elrod’s clients included out-of-state hunters from Georgia. One of these hunters was Thomas Boswell, 39 , of Barnesville, Georgia. Boswell participated in the guided hunts without a Tennessee hunting license and was responsible for the illegal harvesting of five of the deer. The harvested deer would then be transported to Georgia. Fayette County is designated by the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (TWRA) as a Chronic Wasting Disease Zone. Chronic wasting disease is a fatal neurological illness that is contagious to members of the deer family. There is currently no known cure for the disease. Prosecutors charged Elrod and Boswell with violating the Lacey Act, a federal conservation law that bans the trafficking of illegally harvested wildlife. At Elrod’s sentencing hearing on October 21, 2026, Senior United States District Judge J. Daniel Breen placed him on 1 year of probation and ordered that Elrod’s hunting privileges be suspended for a period of 5 years. In addition, Elrod was ordered to pay a $40,000 fine and $20,000 in restitution. Boswell was sentenced in July 2026 and was ordered by Judge Breen to pay a $15,000 fine and $11,000 in restitution. Boswell’s hunting privileges were ordered suspended for a period of 18 months. U.S. Attorney D. Michael Dunavant said, "The U.S. Attorney’s Office is a full-service federal prosecution office, and we have the ability and intention to charge any violations of federal law, no matter where they occur in the Western District of Tennessee. These prosecutions demonstrate our commitment to upholding the rule of law, and to pursuing any cases that harm and impact our rural communities. We commend the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and TWRA for their diligent and thorough work in this successful investigation and appreciate our partnerships with them." “America’s wildlife belongs to all of us. Those who take it illegally put their own interests ahead of everyone who hunts responsibly, values wildlife, and wants healthy populations for the next generation,” said Assistant Director Doug Ault, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Office of Law Enforcement. “Strong partnerships with our state counterparts make this work possible. Together, we will hold those who violate wildlife laws accountable.” This case was investigated by the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency, and the Georgia Department of Natural Resources. Assistant United States Attorney Immanuel Chioco prosecuted this case on behalf of the government. ### For more information, please contact our Media Relations Team at USATNW.Media@usdoj.gov . Follow the U.S. Attorney’s Office on Facebook or on X at @WDTNNews for office news and updates. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Wildlife Component USAO - Tennessee, Western

Federal jury convicts dual U.S.-Jamaican citizen for murder-for-hire and drug-trafficking conspiracy
body: Press Release Federal jury convicts dual U.S.-Jamaican citizen for murder-for-hire and drug-trafficking conspiracy Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Virginia Four other conspirators were previously convicted in this Homeland Security Task Force case NORFOLK, Va. – A federal jury convicted Antwan Denetrick Hue, 42, today on charges of conspiracy to commit murder for hire, murder for hire, murder while engaged in drug trafficking, and conspiracy to manufacture and distribute cocaine. According to court records and evidence presented at trial, from 2015 to 2019, Hue, 42, managed an international drug trafficking organization. Hue and Regina Sade Chen, aka Erica Williams, 36, imported multi-kilogram quantities of cocaine into the United States from the Caribbean, including Jamaica. Hue and Chen employed transporters, including co-defendants Kayla Bedessie, 34, and Deshawn Hassan Mercer, 33, to smuggle cocaine into and money out of the United States. Hue frequently traveled between the United States and Jamaica as well as other Caribbean countries to meet with co-conspirators and oversee the smuggling operation. When Hue applied for a renewal of his expiring U.S. passport in 2016, he was informed that he was not eligible because he was in arrears on child support payments owed to the mother of his minor child. In November 2016, Hue hired Mercer and co-defendant Zquan Leon Steeps, 32, to murder the mother, believing her death would permanently end future child support payments and allow him to renew his passport. On Dec. 4, 2016, Mercer, Steeps, and Denasha Campbell (who is now deceased) traveled to the victim’s home in Norfolk. After Campbell knocked and asked to use the victim’s phone, Mercer and Steeps forced their way into the residence and shot and killed the victim in front of her 9-year-old child. The conspirators fled the residence, leaving the child to call 911. After learning that child support remains effective after the death of a parent, on Dec. 24, 2016, Hue negotiated with the victim’s mother for her to have full custody of his son so long as Hue was discharged from all further child support payments. On Oct. 22, 2018, Hue, citing an urgent need to travel to Montego Bay, Jamaica, applied for and obtained a renewal of his passport. In August 2019, the Department of Homeland Security arrested Hue in Florida as he attempted to take possession of a kilogram of cocaine. Hue faces a mandatory life sentence in prison when sentenced on March 4, 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Chen pled guilty on Aug. 29, 2024, to conspiracy to manufacture, distribute and possess with intent to manufacture and distribute cocaine. She faces a mandatory minimum of 10 years and up to life in prison. Bedessie pled guilty on Aug. 29, 2024, to conspiracy to manufacture, distribute and possess with intent to manufacture and distribute cocaine. She was sentenced on Sept. 8, 2025, to seventy months in prison. Mercer and Steeps pled guilty in October 2024 to conspiracy to commit murder for hire. They face a mandatory minimum of life in prison. Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia; Ian Kaufmann, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI’s Richmond Field Office; and Kai Wah Chan, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Washington, D.C., made the announcement after U.S. District Judge Arenda Wright Allen accepted the verdict. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Joseph E. DePadilla and Brian J. Samuels are prosecuting the case. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Washington, D.C., comprises agents and officers from the FBI; Homeland Security Investigations; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives; Drug Enforcement Administration; Diplomatic Security Service; U.S. Marshals Service; U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service; Naval Criminal Investigative Service; Transportation Security Administration Federal Air Marshals Service; U.S. Customs and Border Protection; Enforcement and Removal Operations; and Washington Baltimore HIDTA, with the prosecution being led by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia. Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 2:24-cr-38. Contact USAVAE.Press@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Violent Crime Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Virginia, Eastern

title: Justice Department Releases Eighth Annual Elder Justice Report
body: Press Release Justice Department Releases Eighth Annual Elder Justice Report Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, the Department of Justice’s Civil Division released its Annual Report to Congress on its efforts to Combat Elder Fraud and Abuse . The report summarizes the department’s extensive enforcement, victim support, training and myriad other efforts to promote elder justice during the reporting period from July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026. This year, the Department pursued nearly 350 criminal and civil enforcement actions involving fraud or abuse that targeted or disproportionately affected older adults. Approximately 96% of the cases were criminal in nature and 45% involved international schemes. These cases named 712 defendants charged with stealing or alleged to have stolen $4,841,305,931 from 711,353 victims. During that same period, the Department also engaged in nearly 1200 public awareness and training events, reaching over 62 million Americans.  The Department also helped to organize and participated in the Never Ever Campaign , a public-private coordinated consumer education effort to raise awareness about government and business imposter scams, collectively reaching over 95 million individuals. The Department continued to develop training and resources to support the efforts of state and local prosecutors, law enforcement, victim service providers, and elder justice multidisciplinary teams. Of note this year, the Department supported the development of an online training titled Toolkit for Law Enforcement and Emergency Medical Services When Called to a Long-Term Care Facility, with over 700 professionals taking the course in the first month of its release.  The Department also continued to actively support older victims, whether harmed by family members or strangers. For example, Victims of Crime Act funded organizations allocated $52 million to elder abuse victim services. Further, the Department was able to return millions to older victims, or freeze millions, through a variety of programs. The Department is committed to advancing elder justice through enforcement, public awareness, resources and training for elder justice professionals, and support for older victims and their families.  The Department stands united in its fight against elder abuse, neglect, financial exploitation and fraud to improve the quality of life for older Americans. For more information on elder fraud and abuse, visit the Department’s Elder Justice Initiative website. If you or someone you know has been the victim elder fraud, please call the National Elder Fraud Hotline at 833–FRAUD–11or or 833–372–8311. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Elder Justice Component Civil Division Press Release Number: 26-1270

title: Convictions through Guilty Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions (October 19 through October 23, 2026)
body: Press Release Convictions through Guilty Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions (October 19 through October 23, 2026) Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico, Héctor Ramírez-Carbó, Acting United States Attorney, in conjunction with our partner agencies in the Homeland Security Task Force (“HSTF”) announce the following prosecutorial results for the week of October 19 through October 23, 2026. The HSTF is a permanent, interagency law enforcement task force created by executive order to combat transnational criminal organizations—including cartels, trafficking networks, and foreign terrorist organizations. Convictions through Guilty Pleas: On October 22, 2026, Steven Nieves-Ríos pleaded guilty to violating 21 U.S.C. §§ 952(a), 960(a)(1), (b)(1)(B)(ii), and 963, and 8 U.S.C. §§ 1324(a)(1)(A)(i), (a)(1)(A)(v)(I), and (a)(1)(B)(i) in Criminal Case 25-393 (SCC).  According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with conspiracy to import 5 kilograms or more of cocaine and conspiracy to illegally bring in aliens. Defendant was arrested on September 12, 2025. SAUSA Cody McKinney in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 23, 2026, Julio Jeury Tejada Contreras pleaded guilty to violating 21 U.S.C. §§ 963, 952(a), and 960(b)(1)(B)(ii), 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(1)(A), and 8 U.S.C. § 1326(a) in Criminal Case 26-265 (CVR). According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with conspiracy to import 5 kilograms or more of cocaine, carrying a firearm during and in relation to a drug trafficking crime, and attempted reentry of a previously removed alien.  Defendant was arrested on June 11, 2026. The court set defendant’s sentencing date for January 25, 2026. SAUSA Cody McKinney in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 23, 2026, José Ayala-Rivera pleaded guilty to Count one in Criminal Case 26-143 (GMM). According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with Conspiracy to Receive, Transfer and/or send Firearms via a Common Carrier without Written Notice in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 371. Defendant was arrested on April 30, 2026.  The court set defendant’s sentencing date for January 25, 2027. On October 23, 2026, Joselin A. Méndez-De Jesús pleaded guilty to a violation of Title 8, United States Code, Sections 1326(a) and (b)(1) in Criminal Case No. 26-343 (SCC) and was sentenced to time served by United States District Court Judge Silvia Carreño-Coll. According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with an illegal re-entry offense and was found in the United States after being previously removed from the United States subsequent to a felony conviction. Sentencings: On October 20, 2026, Sergio Ramírez-Payano was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Gina Méndez-Miró to 12 months of incarceration for possessing a machinegun. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on 2 October 2025, in Criminal Case 25-409 (GMM), and pleaded guilty on July 21, 2026. AUSA Joseph Russell is in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 22, 2026, Yanzie Vázquez-González was sentenced by United States District Court Silvia Carreño Coll to 204 months (17 years) of imprisonment and 10 years of supervised release for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on June 10, 2025, in Criminal Case 25-272 (SCC) and pleaded guilty on July 22, 2026. AUSAs Laura Díaz-González and Andres Orr in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 23, 2026, Carlos Gutiérrez-Santana was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Camille Vélez-Rivé to a term of imprisonment of 120 months (10 years) and five years of supervised release for a federal drug trafficking violation. According to court documents, a superseding indictment was filed against the defendant on February 18, 2026, in Criminal Case 25-462 (CVR), and pleaded guilty on July 21, 2026. AUSAs Antonio Pérez and Myriam Fernández are in charge of the prosecution of the case. These prosecutions are part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio CLEVELAND  - The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio, in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division, announced its comprehensive strategy to oversee federal voting protections and address potential election related violations. As part of a nationwide effort to ensure a secure, transparent, and accessible election process, U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer has named Executive Assistant U.S. Attorney Ava Rotell Dustin and Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Shepherd as the 2026 District Election Officers. They will oversee the northern Ohio district’s handling of Election Day complaints in consultation with the Justice Department’s Civil Rights, Criminal, and National Security Divisions in Washington. “My office has partnered with federal, state, and local law enforcement to maintain election security, enforce federal laws, and address credible threats swiftly,” said U.S. Attorney Toepfer. “If you witness—or have direct knowledge of—suspected election fraud, voter intimidation, or unlawful voting activity, we strongly encourage you to report it immediately.” Key Enforcement Priorities for the 2026 Election: • Protecting Voter Rights : Ensuring that all eligible voters can participate in early voting, mail-in voting, and Election Day voting free from discrimination, harassment, or unlawful coercion. • Voter Eligibility and Enforcement: Monitoring compliance with federal laws regarding voter registration and eligibility. •    Combating Election Fraud: Investigating actionable allegations of ballot harvesting, voter impersonation, or intentional disruption of polling places and mail-in ballot processing. AUSAs Dustin and Shepherd will be on duty in the Northern District of Ohio while the polls are open Tuesday, Nov. 3, to respond to complaints of voting rights concerns or fraudulent election activity. They will ensure that such complaints are directed to the appropriate authorities. For Northwestern Ohio, call EAUSA Dustin at 419-241-0767; for Northeastern Ohio, call AUSA Shepherd at 216-622-3859. Complaints about possible violations of the federal voting rights laws may also be made directly to the Civil Rights Division in Washington at civilrights.justice.gov or by phone at 1-855-856-1247. In the case of a crime of violence or intimidation, call 911 immediately and before contacting federal authorities as state and local police have primary jurisdiction over polling places. Contact Jessica Salas Novak Jessica.Salas.Novak@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Ohio, Northern

title: San Antonio Man Sentenced to Over 15 Years in Federal Prison for Meth Dealing
body: Press Release San Antonio Man Sentenced to Over 15 Years in Federal Prison for Meth Dealing Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas SAN ANTONIO – A San Antonio man was sentenced in a federal court to 190 months in prison for conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of a substance containing methamphetamine, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, Alfredo Landin aka “Fredo,” 28, imported large amounts of methamphetamine, which he called “candy,” from Mexico, and distributed it to numerous dealers in the San Antonio area. Landin arranged to have drivers deliver 10 or more kilograms of narcotics at a time in hidden compartments. On July 19, 2021, the Drug Enforcement Administration and Texas Department of Public Safety found approximately eight kilograms of methamphetamine and 3.5 kilograms of heroin in a car that was on its way to drop narcotics off to Landin in Indian Creek. Landin was arrested on April 19, 2024, and pleaded guilty on March 4, 2025. In June, Landin was sentenced to 151 months in a separate case in which he also pleaded guilty to trafficking methamphetamine. “Alfredo Landin was responsible for importing large amounts of methamphetamine and heroin from Mexico to exploit our communities for financial gain,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “Thanks to the tireless efforts of our DEA and DPS partners, we were able to interdict a large shipment of narcotics just before it was delivered to Landin, who will now spend more than 15 years in federal prison concurrent with another 12 ½-year sentence he is already serving.” “Coordinated law enforcement efforts are critical to keeping our communities safe and removing those who peddle poison in San Antonio neighborhoods,” said Miguel A. Madrigal, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration San Antonio Division. “DEA San Antonio remains relentless in its mission to stay one step ahead of drug traffickers, dismantle criminal networks, and bring those responsible to justice.” The DEA and TX DPS investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Eric Yuen prosecuted the case. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Texas, Western

title: Federal jury finds Indian national guilty of unlawfully voting  in 2024 Presidential Election
body: Press Release Federal jury finds Indian national guilty of unlawfully voting  in 2024 Presidential Election Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas FORT WORTH, Texas – United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a federal jury convicted Indian national Khalwinder Singh Bhengura of voting by an alien in a federal election and making a false claim of U.S. citizenship to register to vote. After a two-day trial before U.S. District Judge Mark T. Pittman, the jury deliberated for several hours and returned its verdict Oct. 27. “Voting in our national elections is reserved for US citizens,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Every unlawful vote undermines the voices of eligible citizens, and this office will hold accountable anyone who undermines our elections. This verdict reflects the jury’s careful consideration of the evidence and our commitment to protecting the integrity of the electoral process in North Texas.” According to evidence presented at trial, Bhengura, a citizen of India, became a lawful permanent resident of the United States on June 29, 2022. He is not a U.S. citizen and has never applied for citizenship. On Aug. 1, 2024, Bhengura applied for a Texas driver license in Tarrant County. In that application, he checked boxes stating that he was a U.S. citizen and wished to register to vote. Based on that application, Bhengura was registered to vote in Texas. Voter Registration Application where Bhengura fraudulently confirmed he was a U.S. citizen On Nov. 5, 2024, the defendant voted in person at the East Library and Recreation Center in Arlington, Texas, in a general election that included races for President, Vice President, U.S. Senate and U.S. House of Representatives. Tarrant County voter info showing Bhengura illegally voted in the 2024 General Election Sentencing is set for Feb. 11, 2027. Bhengura faces up to five years in federal prison and a fine of up to $250,000 for false statements of citizenship in order to register to vote and up to one year imprisonment and maximum fine of $100,00o for voting by an alien in a federal election. Bhengura could also be subject to immigration penalties such as removal from the United States after he serves his term of imprisonment. The HSI Dallas field office conducted the investigation with assistance from the Election Integrity Unit of the Texas Office of the Attorney General and the Tarrant County District Attorney’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew Capoccia and Colin Duffy from the Fort Worth Division prosecuted the case. ### Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Fraud Voting and Elections Component USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Albuquerque Man Sentenced for Drug Trafficking and Machinegun Offenses
body: Press Release Albuquerque Man Sentenced for Drug Trafficking and Machinegun Offenses Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – An Albuquerque drug trafficker who amassed an arsenal of firearms, including machinegun conversion devices, and hundreds of grams of methamphetamine and fentanyl has been sentenced to nearly 29 years in federal prison. According to court documents, on July 6, 2024, Deundalas Gales , 37, was driving at a high rate of speed in Albuquerque, New Mexico, when he crashed into another vehicle. Immediately after the crash, Gales fired approximately 25 rounds toward the other vehicle from a handgun equipped with a machinegun conversion device. Although the other vehicle sustained multiple gunshots, the other driver was fortunately not struck. Gales then fled the scene on foot, abandoning the vehicle that contained 447.1 grams of methamphetamine with 99% purity, and a stolen shotgun. As he fled, Gales dropped the firearm with the conversion device, his wallet and other personal belongings that allowed investigators to eventually identify him. On July 13, 2024, officers responded to reports that Gales was breaking into a neighbor’s apartment and setting fire to his own apartment. Officers found Gales bleeding, wearing body armor and holding a loaded firearm magazine. After safely detaining him, Albuquerque Police Department officers entered his smoke-filled apartment to check for occupants and observed firearms and fentanyl pills in plain view. Investigators subsequently obtained a search warrant for the apartment and recovered 216.5 net grams of fentanyl, 892.7 net grams of methamphetamine, five firearms, a black powder revolver, approximately 500 rounds of ammunition, digital scales and multiple firearm magazines. During the investigation, detectives also searched Gales vehicle that was parked at the apartment. Investigators recovered approximately 204 grams of fentanyl, 112.8 net grams of methamphetamine and five additional firearms, including a machinegun conversion device. As a previously convicted felon with prior convictions for assault, aggravated robbery, and possession of a controlled substance, Gales was prohibited from possessing a firearm and ammunition. Gales pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, possessing and brandishing a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, unlawful possession of a machinegun and being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition. Upon his release from prison, Gales will be subject to five years of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Robert “Eric” Castañeda of the Drug Enforcement Administration made the announcement today. The Drug Enforcement Administration investigated this case with assistance from the Albuquerque Police Department and FBI’s Albuquerque Field Office. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Mexico prosecuted this case. Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - New Mexico Press Release Number: 26-295

title: Box Elder man sentenced to more than 2 years in prison for unlawfully possessing handgun
body: Press Release Box Elder man sentenced to more than 2 years in prison for unlawfully possessing handgun Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana GREAT FALLS – A Box Elder man who previously had been convicted of multiple felonies and was found with a handgun was sentenced today to two years and 10 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, U.S. Attorney Scott Twito said. Celestion Charlie Ortega, 40, pleaded guilty in April 2026 to unlawfully possessing a firearm. Chief U.S. District Judge Brian M. Morris presided. The government alleged in court documents that Ortega, who has been convicted of five previous felonies, was discovered by law enforcement in a Great Falls parking lot at 2:30 a.m. on Sept. 29, 2025, after someone reported seeing him peering into cars with a handgun. Ortega at first pretended to be asleep but then cooperated with officers, who searched Ortega’s vehicle and found a loaded Hi-Point 9mm pistol between the front right and rear passenger seats on the floorboard. Officers then searched Ortega and found a round of ammunition in his back pocket. The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted the case. The Great Falls Police Department, Montana Department of Corrections Probation and Parole, and ATF conducted the investigation. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. Contact Keri Leggett Acting Public Affairs Officer keri.leggett@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Project Safe Neighborhoods Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Montana Press Release Number: 26-278

title: 17 Members of a Drug Trafficking Organization Charged with Drug Trafficking and Firearms Violations in Aguadilla, PR, as part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Initiative
body: Press Release 17 Members of a Drug Trafficking Organization Charged with Drug Trafficking and Firearms Violations in Aguadilla, PR, as part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Initiative Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – On October 21, 2026, a federal grand jury in the District of Puerto Rico returned an indictment charging 17 gang members from Aguadilla with conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute, possession and distribution of controlled substances, and firearms violations, announced Héctor Ramírez Carbó, Acting United States Attorney for the District of Puerto Rico. This investigation was led by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Puerto Rico Police Bureau (PRPB) Aguadilla Strike Force, with the collaboration of the Puerto Rico Department of Correction and Rehabilitation, the Puerto Rico & Virgin Islands High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) and The White House Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP). “Drug trafficking organizations like the one alleged in today’s indictment inflict profound harm on our communities—fueling addiction, poisoning our youth, sowing fear, and endangering innocent lives,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Ramírez‑Carbó. “Today’s arrests send a clear message to those who endanger our neighborhoods through drug trafficking and firearms offenses: You will be identified, your organization dismantled and will pay the price.  We will continue working alongside the DEA and our HSTF law enforcement partners to ensure the safety and security of every community in Puerto Rico. Today’s operation just happens to complement DEA’s Red Ribbon Campaign for safer communities and a drug-free life.” “Operation Los Tíos sends a clear message: the DEA’s mission extends throughout Puerto Rico. No community in Puerto Rico is beyond our reach, and no drug trafficking organization is beyond the reach of justice,” said Michael Mayer, Special Agent in Charge, DEA Caribbean Division. “Through the Homeland Security Task Force, the DEA, and our federal, state, and local partners are combining our intelligence, resources, and operational capabilities to dismantle violent criminal organizations. Our commitment to public safety extends across all of Puerto Rico; throughout every municipality, we will continue working together to protect our communities and bring those who threaten them to justice.” The indictment alleges that from 2022, the drug trafficking organization distributed heroin, cocaine base (crack), and fentanyl, within 1,000 feet of the Las Muñecas Public Housing Project (PHP) in Aguadilla, and areas nearby, all for significant financial gain and profit. The object of the conspiracy was to distribute wholesale quantities and street amount quantities of controlled substances and to traffic illegal firearms in Aguadilla and areas nearby. They operated drug points out of different housing projects and wards in or around Aguadilla. The defendants communicated with each other using two-way radios and cell phones, via instant messaging and social media platforms. Leaders conducted meetings to resolve issues, give instructions, and discuss items of interest to the drug trafficking organization. It is alleged that members of the drug trafficking organization participated in acts of violence, including shootings and murders, to further their drug trafficking operations. The defendants acted in different roles to further the goals of the drug trafficking conspiracy, including as leaders, drug point owners, enforcers, runners, sellers, lookouts, and facilitators. Six (6) defendants are facing one charge of possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime and one (1) of those defendants is facing one count of possession of a machine gun in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. Román García, a.k.a. “Iche” [17] Raynell Caravallo Vázquez, a.k.a. “Raynell” Assistant U.S. Attorney (AUSA) and Chief of the Asset Recovery and Money Laundering Division Myriam Y. Fernández, and AUSA Andrés Orr are in charge of the prosecution of the case. If convicted on the drug charges, the defendants face a minimum sentence of 10 years, and up to life in prison. If convicted of both the drug and firearms charges in Count Five, the defendants face a minimum sentence of 15 years, and up to life in prison. The defendant charged with possession of machine guns in furtherance of drug trafficking in Count Six faces a mandatory minimum sentence of thirty years in prison to be served consecutive to any sentence imposed on the drug trafficking charges. title: Eastern Shore Felon Indicted on Firearm Charges
body: Press Release Eastern Shore Felon Indicted on Firearm Charges Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Baltimore, Maryland – A Maryland felon faces indictment after making his initial appearance in federal court, today, for firearm possession crimes. Theodore Harcum, 50, of Denton, is charged with possession of a firearm and ammunition by a prohibited person. Harcum is prohibited from possessing firearms and ammunition due to a prior felony conviction. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the indictment with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Acting Chief Jamie L. Secrist, Denton Police Department. According to the indictment, on April 13, 2026, Harcum possessed a handgun and nine rounds of ammunition. An indictment is not a finding of guilt.  Individuals charged by indictment are presumed innocent until proven guilty at a later criminal proceeding. Harcum faces a maximum sentence of 15 years in federal prison for possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. U.S. Attorney Kelly O. Hayes commended the ATF and Denton Police Department for their work in the investigation. U.S. Attorney Hayes also thanked Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Arqum Rashid who is prosecuting the federal case. For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md . # # # Contact Kevin Nash USAMD.Press@usdoj.gov 410-209-4946 Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Maryland

title: Fraudulent Document Marketplace Operator Sentenced to Federal Prison
body: Press Release Fraudulent Document Marketplace Operator Sentenced to Federal Prison Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia ATLANTA - Kimani Bracey was sentenced to federal prison for operating a fraudulent document marketplace that provided fake documents used to steal pandemic relief funds and commit other fraud. “Bracey exploited the nation’s struggles during the COVID-19 pandemic by creating and disseminating fake documents that fueled extensive fraud against the government, banks, and other financial institutions,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “My office will continue to hold these criminals accountable for facilitating fraud.” “During a time of unprecedented national peril, Kimani Bracey took advantage of a pandemic and profited off helping others steal hundreds of thousands of dollars in federal funds,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “Years after the pandemic, the FBI and our law enforcement partners continue to hold individuals accountable for committing fraud on the government.” According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: Bracey operated two websites offering so-called “novelty” documents to the public, including fake tax returns, bank records, and employment verification documents. Bracey knew that customers were ordering and using the documents to commit fraud. The FBI traced multiple fake documents created by Bracey to Paycheck Protection Program loan applications submitted to banks, which resulted in over $380,000 in fraudulent loans. Bracey also created fake pay stubs and counterfeit employer verification documents to allow people to obtain loans through fraud, in addition to phony COVID-19 test results. Today, U.S. District Judge Thomas W. Thrash, Jr. sentenced Kimani Bracey, 49, of Simpsonville, S.C., to two years, three months in prison to be followed by three years of supervised release and ordered him to pay restitution in the amount of $386,960.50. Bracey pled guilty to wire fraud on June 26, 2026. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Assistant United States Attorneys Calvin A. Leipold, III and Angela Adams prosecuted the case. Anyone with information about allegations of attempted fraud involving COVID-19 can report it by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud (NCDF) Hotline at 866-720-5721 or via the NCDF Web Complaint Form at: https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form . On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within federal benefit programs. For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Fraud COVID-Related Fraud Financial Fraud Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Georgia, Northern

title: Chinese National Sentenced to Additional Prison Time for Escaping from FCI Danbury
body: Press Release Chinese National Sentenced to Additional Prison Time for Escaping from FCI Danbury Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that XIAOQIN YAN, 32, a citizen of China, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Kari A. Dooley in Bridgeport to 10 months of additional imprisonment for escaping from the Federal Correctional Institution in Danbury (FCI Danbury). According to court documents and statements made in court, on December 10, 2024, Yan escaped from the Federal Satellite Low facility at FCI Danbury where she was serving a federal prison sentence imposed in the Middle District of Alabama for arson and possession of a firearm by an illegal alien. Yan was apprehended on December 10, 2024, and has been detained since her arrest.  On April 10, 2026, she pleaded guilty to escape from the custody of the Attorney General. This matter was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation with the assistance of the Danbury Police Department.  The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Anastasia E. King. Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Firearms Offenses Immigration Violent Crime Component USAO - Connecticut

title: Eagle Butte Man Sentenced to Over 2 Years in Federal Prison  for Assaulting a Federal Officer
body: Press Release Eagle Butte Man Sentenced to Over 2 Years in Federal Prison  for Assaulting a Federal Officer Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota PIERRE - United States Attorney Ron Parsons, announced today that U.S. District Judge Eric C. Schulte has sentenced an Eagle Butte, South Dakota, man convicted of Assaulting, Resisting, and Impeding a Federal Officer.  The sentencing took place on October 26, 2026. Philip Lamar Nordvold, a/k/a PJ Nordvold, age 48, was sentenced to two years and four months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Nordvold was indicted by a federal grand jury in January 2026.  He pleaded guilty on July 27, 2026. The conviction stems from an incident that occurred on May 15, 2025, in the Cheyenne River Sioux Indian Reservation. On that day, a Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe Law Enforcement Services Officer made contact with Nordvald to arrest him on an outstanding warrant.  Nordvold resisted by holding a knife above his head and yelling that he was not going back to jail.  Nordvold was arrested after dropping the knife. This case was investigated by the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe Law Enforcement Services and the FBI.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Wayne Venhuizen prosecuted the case. Nordvold was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Contact usasd.press@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Component USAO - South Dakota
