title: The platform approach to becoming Frontier
body: The platform approach to becoming Frontier Oct 27, 2026 | Judson Althoff - CEO, Microsoft Commercial Business Last year at Ignite, we introduced the concept of Frontier Transformation and how it is different from any technology-led pursuit, because it requires us to focus on business outcomes first. It starts with a simple idea: technology was invented to serve humanity, not the other way around. There is no path where this notion of infinite cognitive compute replaces human purpose. Frontier Transformation is an opportunity for a wholesale reinvention of how you think about your unique ideas coming to life and how your organization can thrive in your industry. Over the course of this past year, we have been leading our customers to focus on the three durable traits that are required for successful transformation: human ambition, intelligence and trust. We are taking a platform approach toward enabling the same: Copilot as the place to call home for interacting with AI to empower human ambition; the Microsoft IQ platform to compound and amplify your intelligence from within while protecting your unique differentiation; and Agent 365 to enable Trust and Observability at every layer of the stack so that you can govern, manage, secure and get business value and return out of the capabilities you deliver. Our latest earnings are another important marker on that journey. Behind the numbers are thousands of customers, partners, developers and employees putting AI to work in meaningful ways. We have so many inspiring stories from our customers that highlight these outcomes, and below are some of our favorites. Empowering human ambition with Copilot Volkswagen has scaled Microsoft Copilot to more than 330,000 employees as it expands the role of AI in decision-making and knowledge-based processes across the enterprise. Building on Copilot Chat adoption that reached more than 300,000 monthly active users, employees are now using Copilot with Work IQ for more advanced scenarios, bringing greater organizational context to decision-making and knowledge-based work . Volkswagen is also working with Microsoft to further scale its Intelligent Data Foundation on Microsoft Fabric to make data easier to find, understand and use across the entire company. With this investment, Volkswagen is demonstrating how companies have evolved from using Copilot as a productivity tool to an operating system to empower human ambition. Following a successful pilot, Fujitsu is scaling Microsoft Copilot across its global workforce of approximately 100,000 . Copilot usage has surpassed 90%, and the company is using the tool to connect employees with specialized agents and business systems. AI agents are already automating roughly 75% of initial responses and triage for a service desk that receives nearly 300,000 inquiries annually , while new agents are supporting work across sales, systems engineering, procurement, finance and accounting. As customer zero, Fujitsu is using Copilot as the front door to a multi-agent work environment and using insights from its own AI adoption to better serve its customers. KOHLER is using GitHub Copilot to transform software development, with one organization improving code releases by 25% and reducing error defects by 75%. These engineering breakthroughs are part of a broader effort to embed AI processes across the company, spanning IT, finance, marketing, supply chain and operations. Microsoft Copilot has reached 98% adoption, saving an average of 2 to 5 hours per month as employees are making informed decisions and getting answers faster in the flow of their work . Employees across the company have also created more than 3,000 agents to date, with hundreds active daily . At Krafton , Microsoft Security Copilot and Microsoft Defender XDR are helping the security team respond to a growing volume and complexity of threats. The global gaming company automated key parts of security operations, from alerting and investigation to reporting, combining Microsoft Security solutions with its own systems and data to quickly gather context that helps distinguish real threats from false positives. This approach is having immediate results: security alert recognition time has fallen by approximately 95% to less than one minute, investigation work that previously took tens of minutes now takes about three minutes and roughly 95% of report creation has been automated . By taking on repetitive work, AI is giving Krafton’s security professionals more time to focus on responding to real threats and making critical security decisions. To accelerate discovery across decades of scientific data, NASA is making complex information easier to explore through Microsoft Copilot. NASA employees are using Copilot to sift through massive amounts of academic literature and streamline daily tasks, and specialized assistants are helping researchers navigate complex Earth science data through natural language, extending access to information that once required significant technical expertise. Hydrology Copilot, for example, can analyze variables like precipitation and soil moisture to help communities better understand water conditions, prepare for droughts and anticipate flood risks, while automatically performing calculations and analyses. To transform frontline work, Williams , a US natural gas company, is using Microsoft Copilot to help employees spend less time searching documents and completing manual processes, and more time on critical field operations. Copilot helps teams generate plans, interpret procedures, assess regulatory requirements, troubleshoot issues and complete safety reporting , while employees can create agents tailored to their own workflows. Demonstrating that the person closest to a problem is often the best one to solve it, one operations technician built an anomaly detector using Copilot that compares equipment data against baseline statistics and alerts teams to potential issues before they become costly or dangerous . Since deploying Copilot, AI adoption at Williams has grown from single digits to more than 90%, helping employees accelerate operations, improve reporting and compliance and identify equipment issues earlier. Bristol Myers Squibb has rolled out Microsoft Copilot to 25,000 employees, reaching 96% adoption , and is now putting AI agents to work across everyday use cases such as document review and project management in support of the company’s mission to bring more medicines to more patients faster. One agent, called RABIT, analyzes meeting transcripts, surfaces action items and delivers insights directly within employees’ workflows. Facing rising patient demand and financial pressures, Brown University Health is using Dragon Copilot to give clinicians more time to focus on patients. The health system adopted Dragon Copilot, and an early pilot across 420 clinicians found users spent less time on after-hours documentation and reported lower cognitive burden . Building on that experience, Brown University Health deployed Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio across departments, which led to the creation of more than 24 AI agents to support clinical workflows, hospital policies, patient access and operations . These AI solutions are not only supporting clinicians in the flow of their work but also helping to improve the patient experience and access to care. Microsoft IQ compounds and protects your intelligence BNY has made AI part of how its employees work through Eliza, its in-house AI platform built with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot and GitHub Copilot – with plans to add Work IQ. More than 300 solutions now run on Eliza, ranging from inquiry management to client onboarding, and 100% of employees have been trained on the platform. Across the bank, that scale is translating into meaningful results: client transaction inquiries are being resolved 80% faster and AI-assisted client onboarding is 20% faster on average . Through the Microsoft CEO Co-Innovation program, BNY also worked with Microsoft to develop an AI research capability with Foundry that investigates complex data issues, analyzes context across multiple sources, identifies likely root causes and recommends next steps, bringing AI-assisted reasoning into processes that have traditionally relied on human investigation alone. Docusign is helping 1.9 million customers across 180 countries turn agreement data into actionable business insights. The company built an Intelligent Agreement Management platform on Microsoft Azure and used Microsoft Foundry to shift from general-purpose models to a system of task-specific models that better understand context . This change allows Docusign to process more than a million agreement documents in a single day, with up to eightfold greater throughput and 90% lower AI processing costs. Foundry also supports a model lifecycle designed for continuous improvement, where processes are fine-tuned before deployment and monitored in production , while also providing the governance and traceability needed to meet enterprise requirements for compliance, visibility and control. Now agreement content is structured data that compounds from within, so organizations can use it to make decisions and automate workflows, knowing their IP is protected. To help marketers create more effective content, Kantar turned decades of proprietary advertising intelligence into action with Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry. Working with Microsoft Frontier Company , Kantar connected its LINK AI platform to its proprietary intelligence, AI models and creative workflows, enabling marketers to evaluate, optimize and generate content before it goes to market. The new approach can process and score large volumes of videos 20x faster while reducing platform operating costs by 4x , helping customers move from insight to action in minutes rather than hours . By bringing its unique intelligence into a continuous loop of observation and improvement, Kantar is creating new ways to help marketers turn insight into better creative and business outcomes. Kinaxis , a Canadian supply chain software company, runs Maestro, its AI-driven supply chain orchestration platform, on Microsoft Azure. Maestro helps businesses make better decisions faster amid constant disruption. It brings together traditionally disparate business data like sales orders, inventory and production capacity with external signals like weather, market shifts and breaking news to give planners a near real-time view of their supply chains . With this unified data foundation, planners and analysts can use predictive AI and optimization models to anticipate demand shifts, evaluate constraints and recommend action, while generative AI agents act as assistants to ask questions, explore scenarios and automate parts of the planning process. With this intelligence in one platform, businesses can understand how disruptions ripple across their interconnected operations, weigh trade-offs and adjust plans as conditions change. Moody’s is making more than a century of credit and risk intelligence directly accessible through Microsoft Copilot, giving customers trusted, protected context for complex decisions. Through a federated connector built using Model Context Protocol, customers can access live, decision-grade Moody’s intelligence through Researcher in Copilot and within Word, Excel and Teams, without copying or exporting the underlying data. A single question can synthesize information across credit ratings, company financials, ownership information and physical risk models, helping customers reach insights in minutes instead of spending hours or days on research and analysis . This brings trusted, connected intelligence directly into workflows where customers make complex decisions. To turn conversations into actionable intelligence at global scale, Plaud , an AI hardware and software company, is using Microsoft Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models and Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to power transcription, summarization and AI inference across long-form audio and multilingual scenarios. Serving more than 2 million users worldwide, Plaud increased transcription accuracy and processing speed by 35% and improved inference performance by 30%, helping professionals turn spoken content into structured outputs and insights . Even as its user base doubled, the company used Foundry’s elastic scaling and flexible deployment models to reduce overall compute costs by 35%, while strengthening its ability to meet security, privacy and compliance requirements across global markets . Rockwell Automation built a Maintenance Copilot using Microsoft Foundry to put decades of manufacturing expertise in the hands of employees . The AI assistant brings together expert knowledge from veteran engineers, manufacturing data and machine manuals, allowing technicians to quickly identify likely causes of equipment issues, see how colleagues have solved similar problems and access step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. At its Singapore factory, the approach has helped reduce machine downtime by 33% and cut servicing and spare-part costs by about 25%. Rockwell estimates it has also reduced the time it takes new workers to learn to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three months . With 1.5 billion passengers riding its elevators and escalators every day, TK Elevator knows that every minute of downtime affects how people move through airports, hospitals and offices. Building on a decade of connected-equipment data on Microsoft Azure, the company created AI agents with Microsoft Foundry that brief service technicians before they enter a building, telling them which elevator, which floor, what the issue is and which tools to bring . After each job, a voice agent records the technician’s account of the work in their own words, with no typing, and adds that expertise to a shared record. With 25,000 technicians caring for 1.4 million units worldwide , TK Elevator is turning each technician’s know-how into compounded intelligence every colleague can draw on. Telstra partnered with Microsoft Frontier Company to deploy an AI-powered Migration Payment Agent that helps simplify one of the most complex aspects of customer migration: reconciling billing and payments across legacy and new platforms. The agent uses intelligence across these systems to proactively identify inconsistencies, recommend corrective actions and create enriched cases for human review, combining AI-driven insights with human-in-the-loop validation to maintain operational trust and governance. Already supporting more than 272,000 service migrations and delivering recommendations at 95%+ accuracy in production , the solution demonstrates how Telstra is applying agentic AI at enterprise scale to transform complex operations, improve customer outcomes and build reusable AI capabilities while compounding and protecting Telstra’s operational intelligence. Agent 365 observes AI solutions across the stack To advance its transformation into an AI-powered organization, Manulife is adopting Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and leveraging Microsoft Agent 365 to govern, manage and secure AI agents at enterprise scale . With Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry supporting its global enterprise AI platform, Manulife is building a foundation for teams to develop and deploy AI and agentic solutions while maintaining standards for quality, security and cost efficiency. AI is already delivering impact across the business, from generative AI solutions supporting more than 110 million customer calls annually to developers increasing productivity by 30% with assisted and autonomous AI capabilities . With agentic solutions and AI-powered workflows already in production, Manulife is creating the foundation to scale AI responsibly across its global operations and accelerate its next phase of enterprise transformation. Insight Enterprises , a leading solutions integrator and top Microsoft partner, is using Microsoft Agent 365 to govern AI agents at scale . As a Microsoft customer zero organization for Agent 365, Insight Enterprises is quick to adopt new capabilities internally and pass those learnings on to clients. With Microsoft engineering, it tested how Microsoft and third-party agents could be observed, managed, governed and secured through a unified control plane. To date, Insight Enterprises has discovered 9,734 agents with visibility into which are active, what data they can access and how to monitor their activity over time. The experience has helped Insight Enterprises build practical AI governance expertise it can bring to customers, including organizations in highly regulated industries. KPMG is adopting Microsoft Agent 365 to manage and secure AI agents across its global organization, providing centralized observability and control as it scales agentic AI . Agent 365 will also strengthen KPMG Workbench, its multi-agent platform built on Microsoft Foundry that coordinates agents across client service delivery platforms. At the same time, KPMG is expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 276,000 professionals worldwide, helping embed AI more deeply across audit, tax and advisory services. Together, these capabilities are giving KPMG the confidence and security to move agents from experimentation into enterprise-wide deployment, while helping clients do the same. Operating in one of the most highly regulated industries, where protecting sensitive customer information is essential, Truist Financial Corporation is using Agent 365 to manage, govern and observe more than 13,000 AI declarative agents across its organization . Truist manages its agent ecosystem with discipline: every agent has an accountable owner and agents are automatically disabled after 45 days of inactivity . That rigor is driving strong retention and adoption, with more than 8,000 agents active each month. Building on this trusted foundation, Truist has advanced its broader AI strategy through their investment of more than 50,000 Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite seats. — Every quarter gives us an opportunity to step back and look at the progress we are making with our customers and partners around the world. What continues to strike me is not simply the pace of change, but the ambition we see from organizations using technology to achieve aspirations that simply weren’t possible before. We look forward to working alongside you on the path to becoming Frontier, and we hope to see many of you at Microsoft Ignite this year in November to share the latest innovations that will enable you to reach that destination. Judson Althoff is the chief executive officer of the commercial business at Microsoft. He is responsible for the product strategy, sales, services, support, marketing, operations and revenue growth of the company’s commercial business, which operates in more than 120 regional and national subsidiaries globally. Facing rising patient demand and financial pressures, Brown University Health is using Dragon Copilot to give clinicians more time to focus on patients. The health system adopted Dragon Copilot, and an early pilot across 420 clinicians found users spent less time on after-hours documentation and reported lower cognitive burden . Building on that experience, Brown University Health deployed Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio across departments, which led to the creation of more than 24 AI agents to support clinical workflows, hospital policies, patient access and operations . These AI solutions are not only supporting clinicians in the flow of their work but also helping to improve the patient experience and access to care. Microsoft IQ compounds and protects your intelligence BNY has made AI part of how its employees work through Eliza, its in-house AI platform built with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot and GitHub Copilot – with plans to add Work IQ. More than 300 solutions now run on Eliza, ranging from inquiry management to client onboarding, and 100% of employees have been trained on the platform. Across the bank, that scale is translating into meaningful results: client transaction inquiries are being resolved 80% faster and AI-assisted client onboarding is 20% faster on average . Through the Microsoft CEO Co-Innovation program, BNY also worked with Microsoft to develop an AI research capability with Foundry that investigates complex data issues, analyzes context across multiple sources, identifies likely root causes and recommends next steps, bringing AI-assisted reasoning into processes that have traditionally relied on human investigation alone. Docusign is helping 1.9 million customers across 180 countries turn agreement data into actionable business insights. The company built an Intelligent Agreement Management platform on Microsoft Azure and used Microsoft Foundry to shift from general-purpose models to a system of task-specific models that better understand context . This change allows Docusign to process more than a million agreement documents in a single day, with up to eightfold greater throughput and 90% lower AI processing costs. Foundry also supports a model lifecycle designed for continuous improvement, where processes are fine-tuned before deployment and monitored in production , while also providing the governance and traceability needed to meet enterprise requirements for compliance, visibility and control. Now agreement content is structured data that compounds from within, so organizations can use it to make decisions and automate workflows, knowing their IP is protected. To help marketers create more effective content, Kantar turned decades of proprietary advertising intelligence into action with Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry. Working with Microsoft Frontier Company , Kantar connected its LINK AI platform to its proprietary intelligence, AI models and creative workflows, enabling marketers to evaluate, optimize and generate content before it goes to market. The new approach can process and score large volumes of videos 20x faster while reducing platform operating costs by 4x , helping customers move from insight to action in minutes rather than hours . By bringing its unique intelligence into a continuous loop of observation and improvement, Kantar is creating new ways to help marketers turn insight into better creative and business outcomes. Kinaxis , a Canadian supply chain software company, runs Maestro, its AI-driven supply chain orchestration platform, on Microsoft Azure. Maestro helps businesses make better decisions faster amid constant disruption. It brings together traditionally disparate business data like sales orders, inventory and production capacity with external signals like weather, market shifts and breaking news to give planners a near real-time view of their supply chains . With this unified data foundation, planners and analysts can use predictive AI and optimization models to anticipate demand shifts, evaluate constraints and recommend action, while generative AI agents act as assistants to ask questions, explore scenarios and automate parts of the planning process. With this intelligence in one platform, businesses can understand how disruptions ripple across their interconnected operations, weigh trade-offs and adjust plans as conditions change. Moody’s is making more than a century of credit and risk intelligence directly accessible through Microsoft Copilot, giving customers trusted, protected context for complex decisions. Through a federated connector built using Model Context Protocol, customers can access live, decision-grade Moody’s intelligence through Researcher in Copilot and within Word, Excel and Teams, without copying or exporting the underlying data. A single question can synthesize information across credit ratings, company financials, ownership information and physical risk models, helping customers reach insights in minutes instead of spending hours or days on research and analysis . This brings trusted, connected intelligence directly into workflows where customers make complex decisions. To turn conversations into actionable intelligence at global scale, Plaud , an AI hardware and software company, is using Microsoft Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models and Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to power transcription, summarization and AI inference across long-form audio and multilingual scenarios. Serving more than 2 million users worldwide, Plaud increased transcription accuracy and processing speed by 35% and improved inference performance by 30%, helping professionals turn spoken content into structured outputs and insights . Even as its user base doubled, the company used Foundry’s elastic scaling and flexible deployment models to reduce overall compute costs by 35%, while strengthening its ability to meet security, privacy and compliance requirements across global markets . Rockwell Automation built a Maintenance Copilot using Microsoft Foundry to put decades of manufacturing expertise in the hands of employees . The AI assistant brings together expert knowledge from veteran engineers, manufacturing data and machine manuals, allowing technicians to quickly identify likely causes of equipment issues, see how colleagues have solved similar problems and access step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. At its Singapore factory, the approach has helped reduce machine downtime by 33% and cut servicing and spare-part costs by about 25%. Rockwell estimates it has also reduced the time it takes new workers to learn to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three months . With 1.5 billion passengers riding its elevators and escalators every day, TK Elevator knows that every minute of downtime affects how people move through airports, hospitals and offices. Building on a decade of connected-equipment data on Microsoft Azure, the company created AI agents with Microsoft Foundry that brief service technicians before they enter a building, telling them which elevator, which floor, what the issue is and which tools to bring . After each job, a voice agent records the technician’s account of the work in their own words, with no typing, and adds that expertise to a shared record. With 25,000 technicians caring for 1.4 million units worldwide , TK Elevator is turning each technician’s know-how into compounded intelligence every colleague can draw on. Telstra partnered with Microsoft Frontier Company to deploy an AI-powered Migration Payment Agent that helps simplify one of the most complex aspects of customer migration: reconciling billing and payments across legacy and new platforms. The agent uses intelligence across these systems to proactively identify inconsistencies, recommend corrective actions and create enriched cases for human review, combining AI-driven insights with human-in-the-loop validation to maintain operational trust and governance. Already supporting more than 272,000 service migrations and delivering recommendations at 95%+ accuracy in production , the solution demonstrates how Telstra is applying agentic AI at enterprise scale to transform complex operations, improve customer outcomes and build reusable AI capabilities while compounding and protecting Telstra’s operational intelligence. Agent 365 observes AI solutions across the stack To advance its transformation into an AI-powered organization, Manulife is adopting Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and leveraging Microsoft Agent 365 to govern, manage and secure AI agents at enterprise scale . With Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry supporting its global enterprise AI platform, Manulife is building a foundation for teams to develop and deploy AI and agentic solutions while maintaining standards for quality, security and cost efficiency. AI is already delivering impact across the business, from generative AI solutions supporting more than 110 million customer calls annually to developers increasing productivity by 30% with assisted and autonomous AI capabilities . With agentic solutions and AI-powered workflows already in production, Manulife is creating the foundation to scale AI responsibly across its global operations and accelerate its next phase of enterprise transformation. Insight Enterprises , a leading solutions integrator and top Microsoft partner, is using Microsoft Agent 365 to govern AI agents at scale . As a Microsoft customer zero organization for Agent 365, Insight Enterprises is quick to adopt new capabilities internally and pass those learnings on to clients. With Microsoft engineering, it tested how Microsoft and third-party agents could be observed, managed, governed and secured through a unified control plane. To date, Insight Enterprises has discovered 9,734 agents with visibility into which are active, what data they can access and how to monitor their activity over time. The experience has helped Insight Enterprises build practical AI governance expertise it can bring to customers, including organizations in highly regulated industries. KPMG is adopting Microsoft Agent 365 to manage and secure AI agents across its global organization, providing centralized observability and control as it scales agentic AI . Agent 365 will also strengthen KPMG Workbench, its multi-agent platform built on Microsoft Foundry that coordinates agents across client service delivery platforms. At the same time, KPMG is expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 276,000 professionals worldwide, helping embed AI more deeply across audit, tax and advisory services. Together, these capabilities are giving KPMG the confidence and security to move agents from experimentation into enterprise-wide deployment, while helping clients do the same. Operating in one of the most highly regulated industries, where protecting sensitive customer information is essential, Truist Financial Corporation is using Agent 365 to manage, govern and observe more than 13,000 AI declarative agents across its organization . Truist manages its agent ecosystem with discipline: every agent has an accountable owner and agents are automatically disabled after 45 days of inactivity . That rigor is driving strong retention and adoption, with more than 8,000 agents active each month. Building on this trusted foundation, Truist has advanced its broader AI strategy through their investment of more than 50,000 Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite seats. — Every quarter gives us an opportunity to step back and look at the progress we are making with our customers and partners around the world. What continues to strike me is not simply the pace of change, but the ambition we see from organizations using technology to achieve aspirations that simply weren’t possible before. We look forward to working alongside you on the path to becoming Frontier, and we hope to see many of you at Microsoft Ignite this year in November to share the latest innovations that will enable you to reach that destination. Judson Althoff is the chief executive officer of the commercial business at Microsoft. He is responsible for the product strategy, sales, services, support, marketing, operations and revenue growth of the company’s commercial business, which operates in more than 120 regional and national subsidiaries globally. title: We’re announcing Genie 4, our new world model for real-time interactive simulation.
body: We’re announcing Genie 4, our new world model for real-time interactive simulation. Oct 27, 2026 Today, we’re announcing our research on Genie 4, our new world model that brings unprecedented realism and native audio to real-time interactive simulation. The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity. With Genie 4, you can set an event in motion and steer scenes in real time using natural language, like moving the camera, changing the weather, or introducing new characters. Every world also generates native audio on the fly, including ambient sounds, music, and interactive dialogue. Simulating the world is a crucial step toward AGI, enabling safe training environments for robots and agents, and amplifying creative tools across industries like filmmaking, journalism, gaming, and manufacturing. We have started rolling out Genie 4 to a limited group of trusted testers. It’s coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and AI Studio. Explore the demos on the Google DeepMind blog .

title: How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia
body: How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration is working with NVIDIA to deploy open source AI tools to accelerate the science that makes new treatments possible. October 27, 2026 by Anthony Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! There are 57 million people worldwide living with dementia today. For the researchers working to help them, the obstacle isn’t a lack of effort — it’s too much data, too few experts to synthesize it and a pace of discovery that can’t keep up with the disease. The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN), working with NVIDIA, is using AI to change that. Alzheimer’s disease is one of today’s leading global health challenges, with over 10 million new dementia cases diagnosed each year. Despite a 7x increase in National Institutes of Health funding in the last 15 years — reaching $3.9 billion annually — no treatment has been found to stop, prevent or reverse the disease yet. The bottlenecks are not enough high impact scientific findings, too much data living in institutional silos and too slow a pace of synthesis to keep up with the research that is published. C-BRAIN, led by Dr. Randall Bateman and a consortium of 18 member institutions across academic, philanthropic, pharma and research organizations, launched in November 2025 to help scientists make better, faster discoveries by accelerating the research that makes new treatments possible. “We have a window of opportunity with artificial intelligence to do research fundamentally different than we’ve ever done before, in a way that accelerates discoveries to help patients,” said Bateman, founder and director of C-BRAIN and the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Distinguished Professor of Neurology at the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. He described their work as “AI tools built by scientists, for scientists.” The consortium is building a system that harnesses previously untapped Alzheimer’s research data to support scientists’ work. Speeding Research From Weeks to Hours Essential assets in Alzheimer’s research are datasets that have never been publicly accessible to AI tools or human researchers. This includes unpublished findings, negative results and governed proprietary data from member institutions. “A lot of life sciences data doesn’t make its way into the frontier models,” said Dr. Ade Ojewole, chief technology officer of C-BRAIN. “The consequence of that is we’re leaving a lot of intelligence on the table.” C-BRAIN refers to this as “dark data,” which slows down Alzheimer’s research. Some dark data is directly deposited into secure computer systems for AI tools to access. To use this data without compromising patient privacy or institutional governance, C-BRAIN uses a hybrid centralized and federated approach — where AI models learn from data at each institution without that data ever having to leave its walls. This kind of infrastructure is technically demanding to build and scale, which is part of what NVIDIA brings to the collaboration. C-BRAIN currently runs 64 NVIDIA data center GPUs on premises alongside cloud-based nodes on Microsoft Azure, with additional NVIDIA GPU capacity, including NVIDIA Blackwell systems , on the horizon as the consortium’s ambitions scale. To explore how AI and accelerated computing can advance Alzheimer’s research while navigating its technical demands, C-BRAIN is working with NVIDIA to incorporate technologies including the NVIDIA BioNeMo open developer platform and the MONAI framework for C-BRAIN’s research pipelines. “The C-BRAIN collaboration with NVIDIA aims to unlock those models in a way that they can deliver something quite impactful and important,” said Bateman. “A great deal of optimization is going to be needed as we push the boundaries of what today’s spatial omics machine learning architectures can model,” Ojewole said. “NVIDIA software is definitely going to come into play there.” Researchers at C-BRAIN have already built two tools: OpenScientist — built with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in an effort led by research scientist Justin Reese — and InsightEngine , built with 387 Labs. OpenScientist is an open source agentic AI co-scientist that takes a scientist’s research question and dataset, then semi-autonomously generates hypotheses, runs analyses and produces verifiable, auditable insights. InsightEngine is an open source research platform that uses agentic AI to test hypotheses against the scientific literature, analyzing user-supplied datasets, exploring a biomedical knowledge graph and checking every claim against evidence to catch hallucinations before researchers commit to costly experiments. In published case studies, OpenScientist completed analyses in minutes that domain scientists estimated would take weeks to months, at a cost of under $10 per run. At C-BRAIN’s current reach of over 200 research groups, this capability could release substantial research capacity, potentially exceeding one million hours annually at scale. From Correlation to Cause Looking ahead, C-BRAIN aims to build a multimodal biological foundation model trained on the full breadth of its data — neuroimaging, multi-omics, fluid biomarkers and longitudinal clinical measures. By year three, it aims to discover new causal mechanisms of brain aging and Alzheimer’s disease, moving to testable scientific principles using the full scope of available research and data. Bateman said, “ AI that can think and reason has the potential to accelerate discoveries that will lead to powerful and implementable preventions and treatments for the entire population.” Categories: AI Tags: Agentic AI AI for Good Healthcare and Life Sciences Open Source Related News AI How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia Oct 27, 2026 AI NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models Oct 21, 2026 AI NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations Oct 21, 2026 AI Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction Oct 21, 2026
retained_feed_body: There are 57 million people worldwide living with dementia today. For the researchers working to help them, the obstacle isn’t a lack of effort — it’s too much data, too few experts to synthesize it and a pace of discovery that can’t keep up with the disease. The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN), working with NVIDIA, is using AI to change that. Alzheimer’s disease is one of today’s leading global health challenges, with over 10 million new dementia cases diagnosed each year. Despite a 7x increase in National Institutes of Health funding in the last 15 years — reaching $3.9 billion annually — no treatment has been found to stop, prevent or reverse the disease yet. The bottlenecks are not enough high impact scientific findings, too much data living in institutional silos and too slow a pace of synthesis to keep up with the research that is published. C-BRAIN, led by Dr. Randall Bateman and a consortium of 18 member institutions across academic, philanthropic, pharma and research organizations, launched in November 2025 to help scientists make better, faster discoveries by accelerating the research that makes new treatments possible. “We have a window of opportunity with artificial intelligence to do research fundamentally different than we’ve ever done before, in a way that accelerates discoveries to help patients,” said Bateman, founder and director of C-BRAIN and the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Distinguished Professor of Neurology at the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. He described their work as “AI tools built by scientists, for scientists.” The consortium is building a system that harnesses previously untapped Alzheimer’s research data to support scientists’ work. Speeding Research From Weeks to Hours Essential assets in Alzheimer’s research are datasets that have never been publicly accessible to AI tools or human researchers. This includes unpublished findings, negative results and governed proprietary data from member institutions. “A lot of life sciences data doesn’t make its way into the frontier models,” said Dr. Ade Ojewole, chief technology officer of C-BRAIN. “The consequence of that is we’re leaving a lot of intelligence on the table.” C-BRAIN refers to this as “dark data,” which slows down Alzheimer’s research. Some dark data is directly deposited into secure computer systems for AI tools to access. To use this data without compromising patient privacy or institutional governance, C-BRAIN uses a hybrid centralized and federated approach — where AI models learn from data at each institution without that data ever having to leave its walls. This kind of infrastructure is technically demanding to build and scale, which is part of what NVIDIA brings to the collaboration. C-BRAIN currently runs 64 NVIDIA data center GPUs on premises alongside cloud-based nodes on Microsoft Azure, with additional NVIDIA GPU capacity, including NVIDIA Blackwell systems , on the horizon as the consortium’s ambitions scale. To explore how AI and accelerated computing can advance Alzheimer’s research while navigating its technical demands, C-BRAIN is working with NVIDIA to incorporate technologies including the NVIDIA BioNeMo open developer platform and the MONAI framework for C-BRAIN’s research pipelines. “The C-BRAIN collaboration with NVIDIA aims to unlock those models in a way that they can deliver something quite impactful and important,” said Bateman. “A great deal of optimization is going to be needed as we push the boundaries of what today’s spatial omics machine learning architectures can model,” Ojewole said. “NVIDIA software is definitely going to come into play there.” Researchers at C-BRAIN have already built two tools: OpenScientist — built with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in an effort led by research scientist Justin Reese — and InsightEngine , built with 387 Labs. OpenScientist is an open source agentic AI co-scientist that takes a scientist’s research question and dataset, then semi-autonomously generates hypotheses, runs analyses and produces verifiable, auditable insights. InsightEngine is an open source research platform that uses agentic AI to test hypotheses against the scientific literature, analyzing user-supplied datasets, exploring a biomedical knowledge graph and checking every claim against evidence to catch hallucinations before researchers commit to costly experiments. In published case studies, OpenScientist completed analyses in minutes that domain scientists estimated would take weeks to months, at a cost of under $10 per run. At C-BRAIN’s current reach of over 200 research groups, this capability could release substantial research capacity, potentially exceeding one million hours annually at scale. From Correlation to Cause Looking ahead, C-BRAIN aims to build a multimodal biological foundation model trained on the full breadth of its data — neuroimaging, multi-omics, fluid biomarkers and longitudinal clinical measures. By year three, it aims to discover new causal mechanisms of brain aging and Alzheimer’s disease, moving to testable scientific principles using the full scope of available research and data. Bateman said, “ AI that can think and reason has the potential to accelerate discoveries that will lead to powerful and implementable preventions and treatments for the entire population.”

title: Jury Finds Man Guilty of Bias-Related Hate Crime for Murdering a Homeless Man
body: Press Release Jury Finds Man Guilty of Bias-Related Hate Crime for Murdering a Homeless Man Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Defendant Targeted Homeless People to Shoot WASHINGTON – Gerald Brevard, III, 35, of Washington, D.C., was found guilty today of bias-related hate crimes in the Superior Court for the District of Columbia, on charges stemming from the murder of 54-year-old Morgan Holmes, a homeless man and attacks on two other homeless men, in March 2022, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “This defendant’s deliberate and violent attacks on vulnerable members of our community represent a grave breach of public safety and basic human dignity,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Today’s convictions affirms that such brutality will be met with a firm and decisive response.” Brevard was found guilty of 16 counts to include first-degree murder while armed, assault with intent to kill while armed, aggravated assault while armed, mayhem while armed, and multiple firearm offenses.  Brevard was also found guilty of bias-related hate crimes based on the victims perceived or actual homelessness.  Superior Court Judge Neal Kravitz scheduled sentencing for January 29, 2027. According to the government’s evidence, between March 3 and March 9, 2022, Brevard attacked three homeless men in Washington, D.C.  On March 3, 2022, he shot the first victim, who was asleep under a bridge on New York Avenue, N.E.  On March 8, 2022, again, while armed with a firearm, Brevard shot a second victim at his encampment on H Street, N.E.  The victim suffered serious and permanent bodily injuries as a result of the six gunshot wounds to his head, chest, and body.  Finally, on March 9, 2022, Brevard stabbed and shot the third victim who was lying in bed in his encampment on New York Avenue, N.E., resulting in his death.  The defendant then set the victim’s body and encampment on fire. All three men were homeless and living in Northeast, D.C. at the time they were attacked. Brevard was arrested on March 15, 2022, and has been in custody since. Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department. This case was investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department with assistance from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives Washington Field Division. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Michelle D. Jackson and Sarah C. Santiago. 2022 CF1 001525 Contact USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Component USAO - District of Columbia

title: Non-citizen pleads guilty to unlawful voting in federal election
body: Press Release Non-citizen pleads guilty to unlawful voting in federal election Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Wyoming usawy.pio@usdoj.gov CHEYENNE, Wyo. — Maksim Sergeevich Shakirov , 29, a citizen of Uzbekistan residing in Rawlins, Wyoming, pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of voting by an alien, in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 611. Shakirov appeared before Chief U.S. District Judge Kelly H. Rankin for his initial appearance and entry of his guilty plea. According to court documents, Shakirov unlawfully cast a ballot in the federal election held on November 5, 2024. “Election integrity is the cornerstone of our Republic. We will not tolerate non‑citizens voting,” said U.S. Attorney Darin Smith. “Anyone who votes illegally in Wyoming will be found out and prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.” Shakirov’s sentencing is scheduled for January 14, 2027. The court will determine the appropriate sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other applicable statutory factors. The Carbon County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case in coordination with Homeland Security Investigations. Assistant U.S. Attorney Lance Johnston is handling the case. Case No. 26-CR-0070. The U.S. Attorney’s Office reminds the public that federal law protects voters from intimidation, disruption, and fraud at the polls. Individuals with information concerning suspected election crimes or voting rights violations may report those concerns to the Department of Justice or local law enforcement. Information regarding suspected election fraud or unlawful voting may also be reported to the FBI by calling 1-800-CALL-FBI (225-5324) or submitting a tip online at tips.fbi.gov . Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Wyoming Press Release Number: 26-051

Shakirov appeared before Chief U.S. District Judge Kelly H. Rankin for his initial appearance and entry of his guilty plea.

title: Seattle restaurant owner sentenced to prison for failing to pay employment taxes for dozens of employees over ten years
body: Press Release Seattle restaurant owner sentenced to prison for failing to pay employment taxes for dozens of employees over ten years Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Spent the money on an expensive remodel, gambling, travel and more Seattle – The owner of a restaurant in Seattle’s Capitol Hill neighborhood was sentenced Monday in U.S. District Court in Seattle to 13 months in prison and three years of supervised release for willfully failing to pay over more than $1.4 million in unemployment, Social Security, and Medicare taxes – some of which were withheld from employee paychecks, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Ruadhri McCormick, 44, of Seattle, owns and operates Single Shot restaurant. Between 2014 and 2024 he employed as many as 87 people as servers, bartenders, and cooks. While McCormick withheld payroll taxes from employee paychecks, he kept the money and failed to pay it over to the Internal Revenue Service.  At the sentencing hearing U.S. District Judge Kimberly K. Evanson said, “This offense involves a significant breach of public trust…  During the period when taxes were not being paid, he was spending on a home remodel, casino expenses, and travel.” “This defendant chose to use money that should have gone to pay for the employee’s future benefits, to pay to remodel a home on Vashon Island,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd. “Unfortunately, the employee’s Social Security work records now show gaps where they don’t have credit for the years they put in at McCormick’s restaurant.” McCormick was ordered to pay $1,446,341 in restitution. For at least thirty-six quarters between 2014 and 2024, McCormick failed to pay $1,027,362 in payroll taxes that had been withheld from employee paychecks. McCormick also failed to pay the employer portions of the Social Security taxes, Medicare taxes, and federal unemployment taxes – more than $400,000 – bringing the total tax loss to $1,446,341. McCormick also admitted in his plea agreement that he did not file his personal income taxes from any tax year 2015 through 2024. The investigation found that McCormick spent nearly $400,000 buying and remodeling a home on Vashon Island, nearly $125,000 on casinos expenses, and more than $38,000 on travel. In asking for a 15-month prison sentence, Assistant United States Attorney Lauren Staniar noted that several employees’ Social Security work history appears incomplete for years they worked at Single Shot, meaning their benefits at retirement could be lower. In her sentencing memo AUSA Staniar wrote, “McCormick failed to pay employment taxes for about a decade—from 2014 through 2024. This crime does not reflect a momentary lapse in judgment. Thirty-nine times McCormick’s quarterly taxes came due, and thirty-nine times he made the conscious decision not to pay them. McCormick also deprived his employees of money they earned as servers, bartenders, and cooks. McCormick withheld taxes from his employees’ paychecks, meaning he reduced their take-home pay by an amount he represented he would remit to the IRS on their behalf. In some sense, that money belonged to the employees’—McCormick was supposed to hold it in trust on their behalf and send it to the IRS for their benefits. But, instead of remitting the withheld amounts as promised, the money sat in Single Shot’s bank account, where McCormick spent it on himself.” The case was investigated by the Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigations (IRS-CI). The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Lauren Watts Staniar. Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Tax Component USAO - Washington, Western

title: Renton, Washington resident sentenced to 4+ years in prison for drug trafficking
body: Press Release Renton, Washington resident sentenced to 4+ years in prison for drug trafficking Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Investigation reveals a known gang member trafficking drugs to homeless encampments and sex trafficking vulnerable victims Seattle – A 40-year-old Renton, Washington man was sentenced Monday in U.S. District Court in Seattle to 50 months in prison for drug trafficking, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Davon Malbrough was identified as a member of the “Family Mafia Crips” – a criminal gang profiting off the distribution of controlled substances and sex trafficking with ties to the unlawful possession of firearms and various violent crimes. In 2023, the Drug Enforcement Administration and Homeland Security Investigations began investigating drug and sex trafficking by members of the gang. Malbrough was spotted repeatedly selling fentanyl and methamphetamine at a homeless encampment in Bellingham, Washington. At the sentencing hearing U.S. District Judge Kymberly K. Evanson said “This is a very serious offense.  The defendant distributed highly addictive drugs to highly addicted people.” According to records filed in the case, on several days in July 2023, Malbrough was spotted at a transient encampment in Bellingham that was known to be a hotbed of drug use and other criminal activity. On three different occasions Malbrough sold fentanyl powder and pills to a person working with law enforcement. In December 2023, a traffic stop of Malbrough’s Jaguar SUV led to the seizure of 10 grams of pure methamphetamine, 3.5 grams of fentanyl pills, 12.6 grams of fentanyl powder along with two drug scales and $1,250 of drug proceeds. In October 2025, Malbrough was indicted for possession of controlled substances with intent to distribute and two counts of distribution of controlled substances. In June 2026 Malbrough pleaded guilty to possession of controlled substances with intent to distribute. In asking for a 63-month sentence prosecutors wrote to the court, “Malbrough was released from prison in late 2018 following his near 150-month sentence for Assault in the first degree. He ended his term of supervised release on October 18, 2022. Less than one year later, he was selling fentanyl to transients in a homeless encampment and trafficking women for profit. The rapid recidivism shows a heightened risk to community safety.” The case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Zachary Dilon and Kate Crisham. Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Washington, Western

title: Texas Woman Sentenced to Prison for Conspiracy to Distribute Fentanyl Pills
body: Press Release Texas Woman Sentenced to Prison for Conspiracy to Distribute Fentanyl Pills Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – A Dallas, Texas, woman was sentenced today by United States District Judge Gloria M. Navarro to 36 months in prison for bringing more than 12,000 fentanyl pills into the Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas and attempting to transport the drugs on an airplane to Texas. The government recommended a sentence of 57 months in prison. “Pumping thousands of lethal doses into our streets isn't just low-level drug dealing—it's a calculation of death for profit,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “A cache of 12,000 fentanyl pills represents thousands of potential overdoses waiting to happen. This sentence serves as a direct warning to anyone pushing this poison through Nevada's communities: federal law enforcement will hunt you down, and you will spend the next chapter of your life behind federal bars." “Protecting the integrity of the American electoral process is among our highest responsibility,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Office. “We will exhaustively pursue and hold accountable anyone who seeks to undermine our elections, ensuring that every citizen's right to a free and fair vote is protected. We will utilize all appropriate resources to investigate credible claims of voter fraud, steadfastly guided by our core values of Fidelity, Bravery, and Integrity. Always remember: Justice will find you.” According to court documents, Aundrea Cymone Hamilton conspired with others to distribute one kilogram or more of fentanyl, a Schedule II controlled substance. On March 18, 2023, Hamilton arrived at the Las Vegas airport with a carryon luggage containing 1321.5 grams of fentanyl she attempted to transport to Texas. During a screening of Hamilton’s carryon luggage, the Transportation Security Administration noticed abnormalities and pulled the carryon luggage for secondary screening. Once Hamilton saw the luggage had been pulled, she left the security checkpoint, exited the airport, and fled to Texas by bus. In January 2025, Hamilton was arrested in Texas. This case was investigated by the FBI. Assistant United States Attorney Melinda Brewer prosecuted the case. ### Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Opioids Component USAO - Nevada

The government recommended a sentence of 57 months in prison.

title: No luck in Wyoming: Las Vegas woman sentenced to federal prison for forged treasury check scheme
body: Press Release No luck in Wyoming: Las Vegas woman sentenced to federal prison for forged treasury check scheme Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Wyoming usawy.pio@usdoj.gov CASPER, Wyo. — Katrina Marie Amaya-Lopez , 47, of Las Vegas, Nevada, was sentenced to 24 months’ imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release for passing a stolen U.S. Treasury check that she falsely endorsed and passed at a Wyoming bank. U.S. District Court Judge Scott W. Skavdahl imposed the sentence on Oct. 20, 2026, in Casper. Amaya-Lopez was also ordered to pay $150,590 in restitution. According to court records, investigators tracked Amaya-Lopez across state lines, arresting her in Nevada on May 1, 2026. “If you bring financial fraud to Wyoming, pack a toothbrush for a federal prison stay,” said U.S. Attorney Darin D. Smith, underscoring the state's aggressive stance on cross-border financial crimes. This case was investigated by the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration. Assistant U.S. Attorney Margaret Vierbuchen prosecuted the crime on behalf of the United States. Case No. 26-CR-00069 This case was part of the Department of Justice's National Fraud Enforcement Division, a specialized, data-driven unit that investigates and prosecutes fraud targeting American citizens and taxpayer-funded programs. The division's operations directly support Executive Order 14395, issued by President Donald J. Trump on March 16, 2026. This order established the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government initiative that implements strict eligibility verification and protects federal and state benefit networks from systemic exploitation. ### Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Fraud Financial Fraud Component USAO - Wyoming Press Release Number: 26-050
